result.summary: Read docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-006.md independently and re-derived rather than trusted TEST-DESIGNER's claims. Re-ran 7 of the spec's file-based script commands directly against messages/ru.json, messages/kk.json, and src/app/globals.css on branch feature/WF02-REQ005-REQ006 (commit cb26ccb3a588...): AC1's key-diff/empty/identical-value script (total_keys:177, empty_kk_values:[], identical_value_pairs matching the 34 named keys exactly), AC2's static Metadata.ogLocale check ('kk_KZ' exactly), AC3a's Kazakh-specific-letter count (569 total, same per-letter distribution), AC4's 8-key status-label source check plus the CSS text-transform:uppercase grep (line 152, .status selector, unconditional), AC5a's exclamation-mark grep (no output, exit 1), AC5b's emoji-range scan (0 matches), and the CFP verbatim-domain-term cross-check (Event/Chapter/Talk/Speaker counts all 0, CFP_count=2). All 7 outputs matched the spec's claimed 'Expected' output byte-for-byte -- none were speculative. No local server was running, so the curl-based rendered checks (AC2/AC4 rendered parts, AC6) were not independently re-executed in this validation pass -- those remain for TEST-RUNNER to run live at Step 4; this does not affect the 3b gate, which checks spec coverage/precision/no-TODO, not live execution. Verified all 3 gate checks: (a) coverage -- every one of REQ-006's 5 numbered acceptance criteria plus the AC6/CFP supporting check has at least one dedicated verification case, each traceable in the spec's own coverage table; (b) no TODO -- grep for 'TODO' in the spec file returned zero matches; (c) precision -- every case names an exact route (/kk, /ru, or explicit N/A-file-check), exact command, and exact expected output/count with explicit FAIL conditions; the two inherently-manual cases (AC5c slogan spot-check, AC6c content-completeness) are as mechanically constrained as their nature allows, naming exact keys/namespaces/viewports/themes/section lists rather than 'check it looks right'. No check failed.
